Came here to suggest SteamOS. It's Debian underneath so you should be able to do whatever you want with it, assuming you know how. I haven't tried it personally.

If not, then I would stick to the more mainstream distros like the Ubuntu family, it seems like most game devs only support that by name. If you want it mostly for gaming, and won't spend much time at the desktop, you may consider a more lightweight desktop environment than Unity which comes as default with Ubuntu - it's a bit of a pig when it comes to memory and such. Maybe try Lubuntu.

Although really, as long as the kernel and graphics stack are fairly recent, you should be fine with most distros. For ease of installation and suchlike, I would tend to stick with distros that use the Debian packaging (apt-get, dpkg, DEB files) I've seen that game devs tend to release deb files. (it is possible to convert DEB files to other formats, but I assume you don't need the extra complication)

I tried steamOS and didn't care for it. Navigation seemed to be designed with a controller in mind. I went with Mint (ubuntu derivative) and installed steam. nVidia driver was a one click gui install. I'm quite happy with this setup.
